title: Senior Data Engineer, Data Platform, Battery Energy Storage Systems
description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Do you want to build the data foundation for a fleet of batteries, from the lab to the field? This role sits where data engineering, software, and the physical sciences meet. You will stand up, nearly from scratch, the pipelines and platforms that carry sensor, test lab, fleet, and model training data across the organization. Every model, algorithm, and design decision we make depends on that data being complete, trustworthy, and easy to use. You will work side by side with scientists, software engineers, and cell experts, and as an early hire you will define how data works across the organization.  
  
This role can be based in Boston, Irvine, Sunnyvale, or Seattle, and involves occasional domestic travel, up to 10% of the time.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Design and build the data architecture for sensor, test lab, fleet, and model training data, from ingestion through storage and access.
* Build scalable, reliable pipelines for high-volume time-series data from devices and test equipment.
* Own data quality, lineage, and governance, so scientists and engineers can trust and reproduce their results.
* Work with scientists and engineers across algorithms, ML, cell modeling, and testing to understand their needs and deliver data in forms they can use.
* Set data engineering standards and tools, and help grow the data engineering function as the organization expands.

  
A day in the life  
Your week moves between design, code, and the people who use your data. One day you might be designing how years of cycling data from multiple labs land in one consistent schema, and the next tracking down why a field data feed is dropping samples. You could be working with a scientist on the data a new model needs, or reviewing a pipeline design with the software team. Some of the best days will be when a scientist finds an aging signal in data your pipeline made usable. Your work determines how fast everyone else can learn.

title: Principal Nuclear Engineer, Safety Analysis
description:
**About Radiant**
-----------------

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running. Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.

**About the Role**  
Radiant is seeking a **Principal Nuclear Engineer, Safety Analysis** to serve as the safety analysis subject matter expert for our Kaleidos microreactor. You will set the technical direction for accident analysis, probabilistic risk assessment, and consequence evaluation, and be the senior authority on how the safety case is built, defended, and maintained. You will lead complex cross-functional analyses, shape design decisions through safety insights, and mentor engineers across the nuclear team. The ideal candidate has deep advanced reactor safety expertise, sound judgment under ambiguity, and a track record of taking safety analyses from concept through regulatory acceptance in a fast-paced startup environment.

**Responsibilities & Duties**

*Technical Leadership and Strategy*

* Define and own the safety analysis strategy and roadmap for Kaleidos, including the approach to licensing basis events, analysis methodologies, and the overall safety case.

title: Strategic Partnerships Lead
description: ABOUT BASE Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. ABOUT THE ROLE We're hiring a Strategic Partnerships Lead to build the partnerships that will help Base become the largest home battery developer and retail energy provider in the country. Our ambition spans the entire electricity market, from homes and small businesses to large commercial and industrial customers. Partnerships will be central to getting there, allowing us to reach millions of customers through companies that already serve them, more efficiently than we could on our own. You'll own the entire partnership lifecycle: identifying the biggest opportunities, building relationships with the country's leading companies, negotiating and closing deals, and turning those agreements into channels that deliver tens of thousands of customers. You'll set the strategy, not just execute it, and remain accountable for each partnership's success well beyond signing. The role covers all partnership categories except homebuilders and land developers, which are managed separately. This is a senior role on Base's small, high-impact business operations team, with broad ownership and visibility across the company. You'll work directly with sales, marketing, product, engineering, finance, deployment, and member experience to bring partnerships to market and scale them. We're looking for someone equally comfortable negotiating with executives at major companies and getting into the details to solve problems and drive results.
